Title: Croton has wilting leaves after repotting

I have repotted my Croton 10 days ago after noticing, that the soil it was in wasn’t really absorbing any water and bottom leaves drying out and dropping every week or so.

It was doing fine, but I noticed yesterday, that leaves started to wilt and I am unsure what to do.

The soil I used this time is 1:1:1 potting soil (fertilized), leca and pine barks.

What I noticed is, that the soil is quite wet (s. Last photo, watering indicator is fully blue) even though I watered last when I repotted the plant (10 days ago).

No, it was in the soil i bought it in before, which clearly wasn’t taking in any water and the plant was losing a bottom leave every 1-2 weeks.

I have humidifiers at home, humidity is about 50% usually

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely cause: the roots aren't taking up water yet, and the mix is staying too wet.** A croton that wilts while the soil is still wet 10 days after watering usually has stressed or damaged roots. Your Sustee confirms the soil is wet: it turns blue after watering and white when it's time to water again. Crotons react badly to change. Drooping is one of the most common signs of croton transplant shock, and changing its location or repotting usually brings on shock and leaf loss. In the photos you also moved it away from the grow light, so it's drying out even more slowly. In a similar case, the soil stayed too wet and some roots died, which is why it wilted even though the soil was wet.

**Other possibilities:**
- **The old root ball is still dry.** If you didn't loosen the old soil that wouldn't absorb water, its core may still be bone dry while the new mix around it reads wet. To check, push a chopstick into the soil right next to the stem.
- **Pests.** The leaf in your third photo has pale speckles, and there's white fuzz on the stem at the soil line. Spider mites leave a stippled, dusty look and fine webbing, and cottony tufts are mealybugs. Check the undersides of the leaves. If the fuzz on the stem wipes off with rubbing alcohol, it was mealybugs; if it's part of the bark, it's not a problem.

**What to do:**
1. **Hold off on watering.** Lift the pot out of the decorative pot, pour out any water collected in the bottom, and slide the plant out to look at the roots. White, firm roots are fine. Cut off any brown, mushy or smelly roots and repot into dry mix. If the old core is dry, soak just that part.
2. **Put it back under the grow light**, or in your brightest window. Keep it warm and away from drafts. More light helps the soil dry and the plant recover.
3. **Water again only when the Sustee turns white**, then water thoroughly. Don't fertilize for about a month, because your soil already has fertilizer in it.
4. **Leave it in one spot.** Losing a few leaves while it settles is normal.
